R1.title: No message leaves the mailbox without a human
R1.statement: The job can read and write drafts. It cannot send, forward, reply, move or delete, whatever the token would allow.
R1.lead: gmail.compose can send. Here is what stops it, and the mutation that proves the test bites.
R1.residual: The Gmail token can send; the allowlist is what stops it.

R2.title: One Scaleway region
R2.statement: Job, secrets, image registry and ledger are declared in fr-par only, with no fallback region.
R2.residual: Serverless inference is in Paris today; the provider commits to Europe. Dedicated Deployment keeps it in one region (paid option).

R3.title: Least privilege, residual risk declared
R3.statement: Each connector asks for the narrowest scope that does the work, and what the code adds on top is written down.
R3.residual: Graph Mail.ReadWrite can delete and the Todoist token reaches every project; both limits live in code. No allowlist stops a stolen token.

R4.title: Monthly rebuild
R4.statement: The image is rebuilt from scratch every month, tested, audited and described by an SBOM before it can replace the running one.

R5.title: Each email handled once
R5.statement: A durable ledger and a check with the provider mean one draft and one set of tasks per email, across hours, containers, crashes and concurrent runs.

R6.title: No content in logs
R6.statement: The journal carries event names, reason codes, counts and hashes. No subject, address, body, draft or secret.

R7.title: Untrusted email cannot steer the job
R7.statement: The model has no tools and picks no identifier. Its output is bounded by a schema and checked; anything doubtful goes to a person.

R8.title: Replies in the sender's language
R8.statement: English, German and Arabic get a reply in kind, right to left for Arabic, in the sender's own thread. Anything else gets English, flagged.
